propositions: A reader cannot distinguish a close with a failed completion-signature append from one closed with the gate off, because gate state is read and discarded without being recorded on the close event.

The completion_expectation enum (8 values: required, disposition, gate_off, gate_unreadable, force_bypassed, local_source, not_certifiable, not_applicable) must be stamped on the *->closed STATUS event in the same locked write as the close, so no additional lock is acquired.
The expectation is computed by _completion_precheck as the second element of a returned pair, consuming the GateState tri-state, with gate-state resolution preceding force-bypass logic.
The idea->closed transition (REJECT/DROP) bypasses _completion_precheck and must explicitly set completion_expectation=not_applicable in close_ticket.

A later reader holding only reduced state and the durable attestation can now discriminate: required+attestation (signed), required+none (signature lost), gate_off (policy choice), gate_unreadable (fault), force_bypassed (--force skipped ENABLED gate), and other enum values indicating no signature was expected.
The field is present-only, backward-compatible, and folded by _fold_close_metadata on both *->closed edges; historical closes without the key reduce to state with the key absent (unknown).
